title: Write a `Function<Employee, String>` that extracts the name, then compose it with another function that uppercases using `.andThen(String::toUpperCase)`.
shortTitle: Write a Function<Employee, String> that extracts the name, then compose with andThen(String::toUpperCase)
keyPoints: Function<T, R>.andThen(after) chains two functions: run the first, then feed its result to the second
f.andThen(g) runs f first then g; f.compose(g) runs g first then f
The composed function is itself a Function, usable anywhere one is expected
Composition builds pipelines of small, testable transformations instead of one big lambda
Types must align: the output of the first function must match the input of the second
Guard against null intermediate values if the first function can return null

s1_definition.oneliner: andThen chains functions left to right: extract the name, then uppercase it.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Function<T, R>** maps an input to an output.
- **.andThen(after)** composes two functions so the first runs and its result feeds the second.
- **f.andThen(g)** runs f first, then g. **f.compose(g)** runs g first, then f.
- The composed function is itself a `Function`, usable in `map()` and other APIs.
- Types must align: the output of the first function must match the input of the second.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya at the National Bank of India first pulls the name off an employee file, then runs that name through a capitaliser. Two steps on an assembly line: get the name, then make it uppercase.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Employee("Rajesh")
       │
       │  getName
       ▼
  "Rajesh"
       │
       │  toUpperCase (andThen)
       ▼
  "RAJESH"

  Pipeline: Employee → getName → toUpperCase → String
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Function.andThen chains two functions left to right: the first function runs, and its result feeds into the second. Define getName as a Function<Employee, String>, call andThen(String::toUpperCase), and you get a single composed function that extracts the name and uppercases it.

The composed function is itself a Function, so pass it directly to map() in a stream. At the National Bank of India, the uppercase-name report used this composition instead of writing one large lambda.

Composition builds pipelines of small, testable transformations. Types must align: the output of the first function must match the input of the second. Guard against null intermediate values to prevent NPE.

Remember one sentence: f.andThen(g) runs f first then g, composing small functions into a readable pipeline.
